_comment: Channel classification rules. The prefixes and exact channel names below are GENERIC EXAMPLES — replace them with your workspace's real naming scheme in a PRIVATE local copy. Do not commit your real channel taxonomy to a public repo: it hands social engineers your internal vocabulary and shows exactly which channels are auto-ignored vs escalated.

client-.label: client-account
client-.notes: Example: client account channels. Default relevant, escalation keywords upgrade to urgent.

project-.label: delivery
project-.notes: Example: delivery/project channels. Blockers need attention even if the user doesn't manage daily delivery.

partner-.label: partner-external
partner-.notes: Example: external partner channels. Client-facing — treat like client channels.

internal-.label: operations
internal-.notes: Example: internal ops channels. Relevant for awareness, escalations are deferred not urgent.

general.label: company-wide
general.notes: Company announcements. Relevant for leadership awareness.

Leapsome.label: hr-noise
Leapsome.notes: Learning path reminders, survey prompts, goal digests.

ProjectX_Daily.label: standup-bot
ProjectX_Daily.notes: Example: standup prompts for a delivery team the user is not on. Replace with your own project standup bots.

HubSpot.label: crm-ops
HubSpot.notes: Deal notifications, closed-won alerts. Relevant for sales pipeline awareness.

Bonusly.label: recognition
Bonusly.notes: Team recognition. Nice to know for leadership.

Google Calendar.label: calendar-noise
Google Calendar.notes: Calendar reminders — already tracked in Google Calendar.

Ashby.label: hiring
Ashby.notes: Hiring pipeline updates. Relevant for leadership.

by_user._comment: Add specific user display names or IDs here for people whose messages always need attention. Format: 'Display Name': { action, label, notes }. Starts empty — populate iteratively based on triage feedback, in your PRIVATE local copy only. Never cache human users without explicit instruction.
